text: the walker judged the drawing, on 296's review page (`docs/findings/walker_review_2026-10-21_drawings/verdicts_2026-10-22/`, asked "Does this drawing read as the building?"): pharmacy_a01's, one storey, "Looks right"; deli_a03's and office's "Needs work" -- "we need to find a way to be simple and not noisy visually". The simpler drawing is carried by 296, which asks what a player scopes out. the walker, on 296's drawings: "assume that in game, a player could rotate it", and what players should see is "simpler but carry all of the signals needed" (`docs/findings/walker_review_2026-10-21_drawings/verdicts_2026-10-22/`). A view a player turns is a model rather than one drawing, and this item's map mesh -- footprints, stairs, openings and holes kept; props, ceilings and tall walls left out -- is that shape; 296 points here for it. the walker's answers on the review page, five of six (2026-10-22 12:11-12:15 UTC, `docs/findings/walker_review_2026-10-21_drawings/verdicts_2026-10-22/`, one document a question): "Does this drawing read as the building?" -- pharmacy_a01 "Looks right", deli_a03 and office "Needs work", deli_a03's note "we need to find a way to be simple and not noisy visually. assume that in game, a player could rotate it as well to"; "Should a facade carry a drawing?" -- "No drawing, as now"; "Is this the kind of drawing players should see?" -- "Simpler", "simpler but carry all of the signals needed"; "Anything a player should see that these leave out?" -- unanswered. The factory's half as this item framed it stands shipped and proven (below); the walker's verdict is that two of the three buildings cannot yet be scoped out from what ships.
